Houses in Brentwood Park, Burnaby: 16 listed at the end of October 2026 and 4 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 25%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. Houses are the smaller part of Brentwood Park: 4% of its 366 listings. Condos and townhomes have their own pages, and the Brentwood Park guide covers the neighbourhood.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Burnaby total for detached houses that month.

blocks.text: Over 5 months 15 houses sold in Brentwood Park against an average of 18.6 listed at month end. In October the community held 3.7% of Burnaby’s 430 house listings.
Houses, condos or townhomes in Brentwood Park?

Most of Brentwood Park is attached housing: 350 condos and townhomes were listed in October against 16 houses. If you are looking at towers near the SkyTrain, start with the condo page; for ground-level homes in a complex, the townhome page.

blocks.text: Brentwood Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

20 houses sold in Brentwood Park with a median price of $1,750,000 (the middle half sold between $1,644,989 and $1,958,500), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 97.2% of the last list price; 10% sold above list. They had a median $699 per square foot, a median year built of 1958 and a median lot of 6,710 square feet.

blocks.text: Brentwood Homes for Sale: streets and boundaries

items.t: Brentwood is a Town Centre core at Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue in the City of Burnaby, not a stand-alone neighbourhood with City-published street boundaries.
The Brentwood Site, guided by its own master plan, sits at the northeast corner of Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue, in the primary core of the Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan area.

The housing streets tied to this page run south and east of the core — Dawson Street, Beta Avenue, Gilmore Avenue, Douglas Road and Parker Street — between the towers and the Brentwood Park Elementary area.

blocks.text: Brentwood Homes for Sale: the housing stock

items.t: The stock on this page is tower-led: high-rise condos around the Brentwood Town Centre and Holdom SkyTrain stations, with detached houses on the residential grid south of Lougheed Highway.
Brentwood Park Elementary, 1455 Delta Avenue, anchors the house streets; Gilmore Community Elementary is at 50 South Gilmore Avenue and Kitchener Elementary at 1351 Gilmore Avenue.

blocks.text: Brentwood Homes for Sale: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Lots with two or more primary units in the R1 District may be stratified, but a secondary suite must stay on the same title as its primary unit and cannot be stratified.

Inside a Frequent Transit Network Area or a transit-oriented area, no off-street parking is required; outside them, a new build needs 1 space for the first unit plus 0.5 spaces per added unit, rounded up.

blocks.text: Brentwood Homes for Sale: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: A rented suite in a Burnaby single-family dwelling carries its own 2026 utility charges — $326.17 for water and $403.00 for sewer use — on top of the main dwelling's charges.
The 180-litre garbage toter is Burnaby's default size, at a 2026 annual disposal fee of $159; the 360-litre large toter costs $447 a year.
Burnaby City Hall and Revenue Services are at 4949 Canada Way, east of Brentwood across the Deer Lake side of the city.

blocks.text: Brentwood Homes for Sale: development and new projects

items.t: Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan and Brentwood Site Conceptual Master Plan amendments, Brentwood Site at Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue, City of Burnaby plan amendment, mixed-use residential and commercial with rental housing, publicly accessible green space and child care: the proposed amendment also redesignates the parcel at Willingdon Avenue and Lougheed Highway from commercial to mixed-use residential and commercial — status: public consultation authorized January 29, 2024, open house held April 2, 2024, finalized amendments to go to Council for consideration (as of November 3, 2026).

R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus extension, Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, TransLink, rapid bus infrastructure with 14 modified stops, two new shelters and three new Burnaby stops — status: construction from end of April 2026 through summer 2026, service began September 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, city-wide including Brentwood, City of Burnaby: the new OCP replaces the 1998 OCP and its land use map takes precedence over the older Brentwood-era community plan maps where they conflict — status: adopted December 9, 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

items.t: 14814, adopted May 12, 2026, including a $0.05920 Growth Infrastructure Investment component.
Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on outstanding current taxes after the July due date and a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

blocks.text: Brentwood Homes for Sale: getting around

items.t: Three Millennium Line stations serve this page's ground — Brentwood Town Centre, Gilmore and Holdom — and the City states its town centres are served by SkyTrain on the Expo and Millennium lines plus high-frequency and local bus routes.
The R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus now runs Park Royal to Metrotown Station through Brentwood Town Centre, with all-day service seven days a week and peak service every 6 to 7 minutes, per TransLink.
Willingdon Avenue is the page's north–south road link, running from Hastings Street south past Highway 1 toward Metrotown and the British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT).

blocks.text: Brentwood Homes for Sale: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lot's Frequent Transit Network Area status on the City's BurnabyMap viewer before pricing added units, because the 6-unit tier and the no-parking-required rule both turn on the 400-metre frequent-transit test.

Check Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status for any edge parcel in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder; the Brentwood core itself is urban, but the check is the official route for any lot in question.
Check the Burnaby 2050 OCP land use map, not the 1996 plan map alone, before assuming redevelopment value near the stations, because the 2025 OCP takes precedence where the maps conflict.

faq.a: The rule route exists: Burnaby's R1 SSMUH District allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots and 6 on lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and multi-unit lots under the district may be stratified. Whether a specific lot qualifies is a parcel read of Zoning Bylaw 2026 No. 14815 — never the repealed 4742.

faq.a: The Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan (1996) is the City's community plan for the centre, and the Brentwood Site at Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue is guided by the Brentwood Site Conceptual Master Plan adopted in 2013. On January 29, 2024 Council authorized public consultation on amendments to both plans to add more diverse housing, rental housing, green space and child care.
faq.q: What plan governs new towers in Brentwood?

faq.a: Permitted forms include single-family homes with laneway homes, duplexes, multiplexes, cottage clusters and rowhouses, and a secondary suite counts toward the total unit count for the lot.
